Bringing a Fantastical Premise to Life

The stars of the independent film *Wicker*—Olivia Colman, Alexander Skarsgård, and Elizabeth Debicki—recently opened up about the unconventional creative journey behind the Black Bear release. Written and directed by married filmmakers Eleanor Wilson and Alex Huston Fischer, the film centers on an ostracized fisherwoman played by Colman, whose life changes when a local basket weaver (Peter Dinklage) crafts her a fantastical husband, played by Skarsgård. When the wicker partner proves to be a better companion than the village's other married men, jealousy and community chaos follow.

For the cast, visualizing the titular character required patience and trust in practical effects. The Weta Workshop designed a complex prosthetic suit sculpted from Skarsgård's features. Speaking to *Variety*, Skarsgård admitted he felt significant anxiety over whether the design would look natural rather than terrifying. However, seeing Colman’s genuine, enthusiastic reaction on set quickly put his fears to rest.

Balancing Comedy and Serious Themes

While the movie’s marketing leaned heavily into its steamy, humorous elements—including promotional items like themed popcorn buckets, splinter removal kits, and woven nipple pasties—the actors emphasize that the film offers substantial dramatic depth alongside the laughs.

Colman noted that the script successfully navigates a tricky tonal tightrope between being extremely silly and deeply heartbreaking. Debicki added that the narrative serves as an examination of marriage, patriarchy, and the societal pressures placed on women. According to the cast, the filmmakers retained complete creative control over the project, allowing them to execute their unique vision without interference from nervous financiers.

Box Office Performance and Audience Reception

Following a buzzy debut after the Sundance Film Festival, where Black Bear acquired the title for $2.5 million, *Wicker* secured a solid start at the domestic box office. The indie film opened in fifth place, bringing in $5.75 million across 1,471 locations. The cast expressed excitement over the strong public response to the film's originality in an era dominated by familiar IP and sequels.
